## Context / Problem

Discovered from livid-painful-mosquito, whose regression test `tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py::test_run_git_encodes_str_stdin_as_utf8` (both `[subprocess-run]` and `[process-group]`) fails in `sweep (windows)` job 135490319213 (run 44503581058, main at 92d3f373e2c): `assert "'550e37cbee0...3e5b7ddb57f0'" == "'6b2b281e114...2db37be95d03'"`. This is a new red entry in the advisory Windows sweep, which is held green so that a red result means a new regression.

Root cause: the test writes `input_data="café ✓\n"` through `run_git` in text mode and compares the blob id with `git hash-object` over the LF-only UTF-8 bytes. On Windows, text-mode `subprocess` stdin translates `\n` into `\r\n` (`io.TextIOWrapper` with the default `newline=None` writes `os.linesep`), so git hashes `café ✓\r\n`. The test's expectation is wrong; the encoding under test (UTF-8) is correct. The subject-decoding cases pass on Windows.

## Approach

Send stdin with no line ending: `input_data="café ✓"`, and compute the expected id over `"café ✓".encode("utf-8")`. That isolates the property under test (the codec) from the newline translation, which is platform behaviour of text mode and not this test's concern. No product code changes; no config key, env var or flag. Portable: the test then has no line-ending dependence.

## Scope

- `tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py`: the stdin case's input and expectation.

## Testing

`pytest tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py` passes on macOS (6 tests). A `sweep (windows)` run on main after the merge shows neither stdin case in its failures.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [x] `pytest tests/unit/test_git_ssh_output_encoding.py` passes, and `make verify` passes.
- [x] [non-codebase] A `sweep (windows)` job on main after the merge does not list `test_run_git_encodes_str_stdin_as_utf8` among its failures. Evidence: run id and job id in a ticket comment.
  provenance: environment=GitHub Actions windows-latest runner (navapbc/rebar test.yml); principal=workflow_dispatch by the session's gh credential; privilege_posture=read-only CI run; instrument=gh run view --job <id> --log — only the Windows sweep runs the test on Windows.
